earlier_scan.source_named: Retired ISO code rmr, split 2010 into Calo [rmq] and Erromintxela [emx]; bookkeeping languoid with no descriptive sources of its own

new_statements.quote: V tomto ohledu jsme si vědomi určité nejednotnosti, kterou snad lze částečně omluvit tím, že problematiku přízvuku v iberských pararomštinách ponecháváme na případnou budoucí studii. K tomuto tématu lze prozatím obecně konstatovat, že pravděpodobný raně romský přízvuk je v iberských (para)romštinách poměrně dobře doložen, což dokládají např. četná adjektiva v caló končící přízvučnou samohláskou.
new_statements.translation: In this respect we are aware of a certain inconsistency, which can perhaps be partly excused by the fact that we leave the problem of stress in the Iberian Para-Romani varieties to a possible future study. On this topic it can for now be stated in general that the probable Early Romani stress is fairly well attested in the Iberian (Para-)Romani varieties, as shown e.g. by the numerous adjectives in Caló ending in a stressed vowel.

Vzájemné ovlivňování romštiny, španělštiny a dalších jazyků Pyrenejského poloostrova [The mutual influence of Romani, Spanish and the other languages of the Iberian Peninsula]. new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule is stated. The only first-hand remark says stress in Iberian Para-Romani (Caló, Catalan and Basque Para-Romani) is left for future study, that older Caló sources often omit accent marks, and that the inherited Early Romani stress (final stress in inherited stems, e.g. Caló adjectives ending in a stressed vowel) is fairly well preserved. Caló otherwise uses Spanish phonology and morphosyntax (Gamella et al. 2011 p. 6, citing Bakker & Courthiade 1991), so word stress is lexically fixed per item as in Spanish, with Romani-origin items keeping their inherited (often final) stress. Provisional reading only; confidence low.
new_statements.exceptions: Krinková 2013 elsewhere notes stress shifts in individual suffixes: -unó > -úno (p. 158 fn. 265) and -edér > -eta 'posunu přízvuku' (p. 158).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, on citation forms drawn from written sources (19th-century vocabularies); no phrase-level or spoken-corpus data. Statement covers Spanish Caló primarily and 'Iberian (Para-)Romani' generally; nothing specific to Erromintxela.
new_statements.identity_note: calo1235 is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for the retired ISO 639-3 code rmr, split by change request 2009-031 (adopted 2010-01-18) into Caló [rmq] = calo1236 (Spanish Para-Romani: Romani lexicon on Spanish phonology and grammar) and Erromintxela [emx] = erro1240 (Basque Para-Romani). It has no descriptive literature of its own; the quoted statement (Krinková 2013 p. 69) describes Iberian Para-Romani generally and Spanish Caló in particular, and is already held under calo1236. Per the code-currency gate (retired codes confer no identity) this key should not get its own catalog row; any entry belongs under calo1236, with erro1240 still lacking any stress statement (Bakker 1991 / Ackerley 1929 not opened).

sources.note: Explicitly leaves the stress problem of Iberian Para-Romani to a future study; notes older Caló sources often omit accents; states the probable Early Romani stress is fairly well preserved in the Iberian (Para-)Romani varieties, e.g. many Caló adjectives ending in a stressed vowel. No rule given.

sources.citation: Borrow, George. 1841. The Zincali: an account of the Gypsies of Spain. London: Murray (Project Gutenberg #565).
sources.note: Ethnography plus Caló vocabulary; no remark on word stress (grep accent/pronunc/stress finds only non-linguistic uses).
English article phonology section is segmental only (from Baudrimont); Basque article infobox labels it 'hizkuntza azentuala' with no elaboration. Both bibliographies checked for primary sources.

sources.citation: Gamella, Juan F., Cayetano Fernández, Magdalena Nieto & Ignasi-Xavier Adiego. 2011. La agonía de una lengua. Lo que queda del caló en el habla de los gitanos. Parte I. Gazeta de Antropología 27(2), art. 39. 45 pp.
sources.note: PDF p. 6: caló is a Para-Romani language, 'un idioma mixto formado por un léxico de origen romaní que usa la fonología y la morfosintaxis de la lengua dominante' (citing Bakker & Courthiade 1991); no stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2009. Change Request Number 2009-031: split [rmr] Caló into [rmq] Caló and [emx] Erromintxela (adopted 2010-01-18). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Administrative form only; rationale for split (Erromintxela grammar Basque-based, Romani component Kalderash-based); cites Agirrezabal 2003, Krutwig 1986, Vizarraga 2001. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Adiego, Ignasi-Xavier. 2004. Del romaní comú als calós ibèrics. Llengua & Literatura 15: 211-236.
sources.note: Comparative Common Romani > Iberian calós; accent-marked citation forms (eraxáj, dinjár, aračí, báste) but no statement on word stress (per calo1236; grep accent/tònic/àton empty apart from '-o àtona' loan-integration remark p. 216).

sources.citation: Quindalé, Francisco [F. de Sales Mayo]. 1870. El gitanismo: historia, costumbres y dialecto de los gitanos, con un epítome de gramática gitana. Madrid: Suárez.
sources.note: Epítome de gramática gitana pp. 49-76: says Caló has the same orthography and grammatical structure as Castilian; no explicit stress rule.
